title: Quarter the optimizer batch (2^19 -> 2^17 tokens/step)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**17 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64, so grad_accum stays 1; all LRs and schedules untouched.
reflection: val_bpb 0.996770 vs 0.997359 baseline: a real but small improvement (-0.00059) from 4x the optimizer steps (3188 steps, 418M tokens, 33.6% MFU, 22.7GB peak VRAM). The batch axis is directionally right but nearly flat -- we paid a visible throughput cost (MFU 33.6%, and 2^17 means per-step optimizer/launch overhead is now a third of step time at ~85ms/step with ~25ms of that not fwd/bwd) and still only bought 0.0006 bpb. That says the baseline was mildly past the critical batch size, not wildly so, and that further cuts will lose to overhead. Combined with a1/a2's 2^18 point this gives the group a 3-point curve; if 2^18 lands at or below my number, 2^18 is the sweet spot and the whole axis should be considered closed at roughly -0.001 bpb total. The more useful finding for later rounds is what the run.log shows about where the time goes: MFU is only ~34% and step time is noisy (79ms best vs 170ms spikes), so there is more headroom in throughput than in this hyperparameter.
note_lr: LRs deliberately not rescaled, so this is a clean single-variable read; a follow-up could trim Adam LRs by ~0.5x at this batch.
